The plan and entrance views establish exposed concrete structure, distinct sports bays, passage on the south and seating integrated with planting on the north. Visible wayfinding assigns Shared Way to the through-route and Activity Floor to the sports area. Perspective occlusion is allowed; reversed zoning, concealed or replaced concrete structure, misplaced labels or seating that blocks the route fails.

Read the schedules, dimensions and relevant details against the records: Shared Way and approaches use broom-finished concrete; Service Strip uses brushed concrete and flush steel grating; basketball uses acrylic-coated asphalt; tennis and fitness use wet-pour rubber over concrete. Planters are freestanding precast concrete, 600 mm high, with 450 mm growing medium and internal drip irrigation; seats use timber slats on freestanding steel frames. Basketball mesh is freestanding and 3,000 mm high, and other new fixtures are freestanding and no higher than 3,000 mm above local ground. The transverse drawing retains 1,200 mm square column shafts and centred 2,400 mm foundations; bridge coverage begins at y = 6,000 mm and its underside is z = 6,240 mm above the southwest datum. Relevant information may be distributed across these sheets; contradictory assemblies, structural attachments or dimensions fail.

Read any operating annotations as records: access is daily 06:00–22:00, sports are daily 08:00–21:00, and passage lighting operates from dusk until 22:00. Depicted use must agree: the 10:00 scene permits active sport and crossing, while 21:30 retains lit public passage and inactive sports equipment. These image roles need not print an hours table, but conflicting stated hours, a closed night through-route or active night sport fails.

The 72 m east–west by 24 m north–south plan uses southwest origin and bands spanning the full width: Shared Way y = 0–4 m, 288 m²; Service Strip y = 4–5.5 m, 108 m²; Activity Floor y = 5.5–21 m, 1,116 m²; Garden Edge y = 21–24 m, 216 m². Areas total 1,728 m² without gaps or double counting. Keep 4 m clear passage between both entrances. Basketball occupies x = 16–32 m, y = 7.5–19.5 m; tennis occupies x = 40–46 m and 46–52 m, both y = 8–18 m; fitness occupies x = 64–70 m, y = 8–18 m. Show one basketball hoop, one table in each tennis envelope, one pull-up station and two stretching rails, with spectators and approaches outside the equipment envelopes. Graphic notation may vary; missing, duplicated, shifted or obstructed programme fails.

Plan evidence locates six column centres at x = 12, 36 and 60 m crossed with y = 8 and 20 m, each inside a centred 4 m square kept clear for maintenance. Drainage runs the full site length at y = 4.5–4.8 m with a flush grated cover. The transverse section cuts x = 36 m and shows the route, drainage, intersected foundations and Garden Edge, explicitly labelling a northward 1% rise, minimum 6,000 mm clearance and maximum 3,000 mm fixture height. Sections and local details need show only intersected or relevant infrastructure, with locations traceable to the plan; encroachments, displaced drainage or inconsistent labels fail.

Both sheets legibly identify the site, four zones and three species. Read DF as Dryopteris filix-mas, CP as Carex pendula and GM as Geranium macrorrhizum. Six 6 m × 2 m beds occupy y = 22–24 m and x = 4–10, 16–22, 28–34, 40–46, 52–58 and 64–70 m. Each bed contains DF 12, CP 16 and GM 20, producing totals 72, 96 and 120 and 72 m² planted area. A keyed schedule is acceptable; mismatched codes, incorrect arithmetic, omitted beds or relocated planting fails.

Provide two readable, dimensioned details identifying the basketball enclosure edge and Shared Way–Service Strip interface. Locate the enclosure within B1 and resolve the route edge and flush drainage relationship without reducing the clear route or intruding into protection zones. Material callouts must agree with the paving schedule. Detail scale and notation may vary; an undimensioned sketch, missing interface, out-of-envelope enclosure or material contradiction fails.

The daytime camera looks into the site from the east entrance and the night camera from the west entrance. Match visible columns, equipment, beds and light locations to the plan, allowing perspective and occlusion. Daytime shows active sport and pedestrian/cycle passage; night shows occupied, illuminated passage with sports facilities inactive. Reversing entrance views, changing the built arrangement or depicting the wrong operating state fails.

The drawing includes a readable north arrow, scale bar, boundary dimension strings, four area labels, sports-envelope outlines, protected column footprints, planting codes and identifiable lighting locations. Any coherent graphic convention is acceptable; missing or illegible required annotations fail.

Sections, interfaces and planting resolve the same plan geometry, protected infrastructure and circulation without conflicting locations or dimensions. Surface assemblies, freestanding fixtures and six-bed planting comply with the site records wherever represented.

Opposite entrance views depict one completed spatial arrangement with consistent structure, sports facilities, planting, materials and lighting. Daytime occupation and illuminated late passage follow the stated sports and access periods.
